checks.claim: By weight, asphalt is about 95 percent stone, sand and gravel, glued by about 5 percent asphalt binder.
checks.why: National Academies and GlobalSpec give 95% aggregate and 5% binder by weight; FHWA gives 5 to 6 percent binder; by volume it differs, so say by weight.

sources.title: Asphalt Road Surfacing Materials Information - GlobalSpec

checks.claim: Poor drainage is one of the most common causes of road failure.
checks.why: A Missouri DOT study calls inadequate drainage the most common cited cause; FHWA guidance designs drains to remove free water from the base. 'Main enemy' is stronger than the sources.

checks.claim: A road is built in layers: compacted subgrade, a crushed stone base, then an asphalt surface
checks.why: Pavement Interactive and Caltrans describe surface course, aggregate base and subgrade.
